name: Robert M. Davis

career.title: Positions of increasing responsibility over more than 14 years
Corporate Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
Corporate Vice President and President of the Renal business, then of the Medical Products business
Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (expanded in 2016 to lead Global Services incl. IT and procurement)
Chief Executive Officer (Chairman of the Board from Dec. 1, 2022)

background_rationale: Built his career in corporate finance, serving as Baxter's treasurer and CFO and then as Merck's CFO before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Merck agreed to acquire Prometheus Biosciences for $200 per share in cash, a total equity value of about $10.8 billion, to strengthen its immunology pipeline.
Merck agreed to acquire Verona Pharma, maker of the COPD maintenance treatment Ohtuvayre, for about $10 billion.

Merck reached an agreement with the U.S. government to offer certain diabetes medicines at about 70% off list price via a direct-to-patient program, alongside a three-year delay on Section 232 tariffs and a commitment of more than $70 billion in U.S. capital and R&D spending.
Merck agreed to acquire Terns Pharmaceuticals for about $6.7 billion in equity value, adding a candidate treatment for chronic myeloid leukemia.

personal_story.hook: A finance-trained lawyer, Rob Davis rose through treasury and CFO roles to run one of the world's largest drugmakers.
personal_story.summary: Davis earned a bachelor's degree in finance from Miami University, then both an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg school and a law degree from Northwestern. He spent more than 14 years at Eli Lilly before moving to Baxter in 2004, where he served as treasurer and CFO and then ran its renal and medical products businesses. He joined Merck as CFO in 2014, took on its global services functions in 2016, and was named president in April 2021 before becoming CEO that July.
